headline: Tyler Higbee (TE-LAR) ruled out with chest bruise
body: Higbee is considered week-to-week, and his status for Thursday's game won't be known until the Rams resume practicing during Week 13 prep. The Rams are already expected to be without Davis Allen (ankle) for multiple weeks, and the absence of Higbee would leave Colby Parkinson and Max Klare as the team's top options at tight end against Kansas City.

headline: Davante Adams (WR-LAR) placed on IR after hamstring surgery
body: Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Saturday that Adams hasn't suffered a setback in his recovery from a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver has not progressed enough to be cleared to return to practice, per Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site. With Adams out for at least one more game, his next opportunity to take the field will be Week 14 against the 49ers on Sunday, Dec. 13. In the absence of both Adams and Puka Nacua (knee, IR), the Rams' top wide receivers for Week 13 will be Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

headline: Noah Fant (TE-NO) questionable with calf injury
body: Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. The 29-year-old Fant has scored either three or four touchdowns in six of his eight NFL regular seasons, including three apiece in 2025 with Cincinnati and so far in 2026 with New Orleans. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp is the next tight end up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

headline: Jalen McMillan (WR-TB) placed on IR with PCL sprain
body: McMillan was listed as a full participant on Thursday's estimated practice report before having his reps limited during Friday's session. The third-year wide receiver has been on injured reserve since suffering an MCL sprain in Week 3, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Monday's NFC South showdown against the Panthers. Given his extended absence, McMillan would likely operate as the Buccaneers' WR4 in his potential return behind Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka and rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst.

headline: Caleb Williams (QB-CHI) questionable with abdomen bruise
body: Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

headline: Denzel Boston (WR-CLE) questionable with quadriceps injury
body: With Boston now on track to log a trio of 'DNP' listings this week, his status for Sunday night's game against the Raiders is cloudy. Friday's final injury report will reveal whether the Browns' starting WR has any chance to play versus Las Vegas or is ruled out ahead of Week 12 action.

headline: Brock Purdy (QB-SF) ruled out with ankle injury
body: Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

headline: Brenen Thompson (WR-LAC) doubtful with hamstring injury
body: Thompson has not played since Week 2 against the Raiders due to a hamstring injury, and it looks like that trend will continue after the rookie fourth-rounder missed all three practices during Week 12 prep. Assuming he doesn't play Sunday, Thompson's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.
